newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Polifarbs still keen on merger, fear delay.
newsitem.headline: Polish Polifarbs still keen on merger, fear delay.

text.p: Polish paintmakers Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw said on Tuesday a treasury ministry demand of a new Wroclaw share issue might delay a planned merger of the two firms.

On Monday Polifarb Wroclaw reported that the Treasury Ministry, controlling about 16 percent of its shares, requested an extraordinary meeting and a new bonus issue of between 6.375 million and 10 million shares.

The move would shift the control of the planned new company in favour of Wroclaw shareholders after Cieszyn shareholders increased their planned bonus issue to give them bigger control of the new firm than the originally planned 50-50 control.
"It (the treasury decision) is certainly a complication and certainly a delay," Polifarb Cieszyn spokesman Jacek Nagorniewicz told Reuters.

Wroclaw President Edward Platek said that if the ministry, which had yet to present detailed drafts for a prospective shareholders meeting, upheld its proposal, the meeting could take place after May 20 at the earliest.
"If the shareholders of the two companies failed to reach a compromise they will lose because the merger will clearly benefit shareholders of both firms," Platek said.
The ministry declined comment on its proposal.
Cieszyn's Nagorniewicz said his company would wait for the final Wroclaw decision and might be forced to call another shareholders' meeting to allow them make a decision of the merger plan's future.
"If Polifarb Wroclaw decides along the lines of the Treasury Ministry proposal I suppose we will have to have our shareholders decide on the further merger plan," he said.

Last month Cieszyn shareholders approved a version of the merger giving them 53.5 percent rather than 50 percent of the new firm by increasing a planned pre-merger bonus issue for Cieszyn shareholders to 6.375 from 2.98 million shares.
Cieszyn currently has 19,125,000 shares, 2,978,820 fewer than Wroclaw and a new bonus issue was originally designed to make up for the difference.
